long_biography.plain_text:
Before property defined his public profile, Rolf Visser specialised in companies that needed rescuing. With university friend Bart Hartman, he built a group that bought underperforming businesses, restructured them and sold them on. Visser also turned that operating experience into doctoral research on how buyers assess troubled companies, making the practice itself part of his professional identity.

KNSF became the deal that joined those takeover skills to real estate. Visser acquired the Dutch state's stake in the explosives company and later secured the remaining shares, becoming sole shareholder. When manufacturing ended, the company's industrial sites became long-horizon redevelopment projects. In Muiden, the former factory grounds were remade as a residential district, while another site supported commercial development.
